strategy.summary: Build pandas from source at buggy commit 9bc2fcf7171b with the test patch applied, then run only test_isin_mismatched_reso. On the buggy revision the (s,ns), (ms,us) and (us,ns) cases for both M and m should fail because a finer-unit value truncates onto a coarser value and matches; on the fixed revision all eight cases should pass. The (ns,s) cases pass on both revisions and do not decide the transition.

system_packages: a C/C++ compiler toolchain (gcc or clang)
pinned_because: No dependency has a documented version constraint in the README (NumPy, python-dateutil, tzdata, Cython are all unbounded), and no era ceiling is recorded, so no pins are relied on; the strategy chooses current releases that build the buggy revision and says so.
Build deps (meson-python, Cython, versioneer) are needed because --no-build-isolation requires them preinstalled; their versions are unconstrained by evidence.

strategy.reproducing_test: pandas/tests/arrays/test_datetimelike.py::test_isin_mismatched_reso parametrized over dtype_kind in [M, m] and (self_unit,val_unit) in [(s,ns),(ms,us),(us,ns),(ns,s)]; builds DatetimeArray/TimedeltaArray via _from_sequence with explicit np dtype M8/m8 at each unit, calls arr.isin(vals), and compares to np.array([False, False]) with tm.assert_numpy_array_equal.
strategy.success_criterion: Buggy revision: the (s,ns), (ms,us) and (us,ns) cases for both M and m FAIL (isin returns [True, False] because the finer value is truncated to the coarser unit and matches element 0), while (ns,s) passes. Fixed revision: all eight cases PASS because values are cast up to the finer resolution via _ensure_matching_resos and no false match occurs.
strategy.numerical_probe: python -c "import pandas as pd; dta=pd.array(pd.to_datetime(['2020-01-01']).as_unit('s')); v=pd.array(pd.to_datetime(['2020-01-01 00:00:00.000000001']).as_unit('ns')); print(dta.isin(v))"
risks: The defect is a pure resolution-conversion path in pandas' Python/Cython datetimelike code and is not stated to depend on platform, architecture, compiler or threading; no sanitizer is needed, but the buggy behaviour is only evidenced on the reporter's build, so a non-transition on a different platform would not refute the plan.
If pip installs a prebuilt pandas wheel instead of building the checked-out source, the test will run against the wrong code and will not transition; the editable source build is required.
NumPy ABI mismatch: the Cython extensions must be built against the same NumPy that runs the tests, so build after installing numpy.
The (ns,s) parametrizations pass on both revisions and provide no transition evidence; the transition rests on the three finer-value cases per dtype_kind.
The test diff is a patch against the buggy revision; if it fails to apply cleanly the reproducing test is absent and the transition cannot be observed.
Test expects the float-free exact integer comparison; no tolerance is involved, so no tolerance-sensitive behaviour is assumed.

oracle.reference_source: Expected array np.array([False, False]) hard-coded in test_isin_mismatched_reso, justified by the 1 in self_unit != 1 in val_unit comparison
oracle.why: isin uses exact integer-based matching on the underlying int64 representation, so exact equality of the boolean array is the correct oracle.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: For (s,ns), the buggy code downcasts the 1 ns value to s, which truncates to 0 s; the result is [True, False] rather than [False, False], so tm.assert_numpy_array_equal raises an AssertionError on the first element.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: With _ensure_matching_resos casting both arrays to ns, the values 0 and 1 in self compare against 1 ns without truncation, giving [False, False] and the assertion holds.
